title: An Ensemble MLP-RF Model for the Prediction of DG-MOSFETs: Addressing Fabrication Process Variations
problem: Accurately predicting Double-Gate MOSFET (DG-MOSFET) electrical characteristics (drain current, gate-source capacitance, drain-gate capacitance) across process variations is time-consuming when using TCAD simulation. ML-based prediction can accelerate device characterization.
motivation: Device characterization via TCAD is computationally expensive and limits design iteration cycles. ML models offer potential speedup as surrogate to simulation while capturing process variation effects.
method: The method combines two machine learning techniques—a multilayer perceptron (a neural network with multiple layers) and a random forest (an algorithm that builds many decision trees and averages their predictions)—to forecast three electrical properties of double-gate MOSFETs: drain current (how much current flows through), gate-source capacitance (electrical storage between gate and source), and drain-gate capacitance (electrical storage between drain and gate), based on device dimensions and manufacturing variations. A separate classification model predicts channel length from devices with unknown specifications. Accuracy is measured using MSE (mean squared error), RMSE (root mean squared error), and R² (proportion of variation explained).
key_novelty: This is the first approach combining a multilayer perceptron and random forest to predict double-gate MOSFET electrical behavior across manufacturing process variations.
contributions: Novel MLP-RF ensemble model for DG-MOSFET characteristics prediction
Demonstrated outstanding accuracy in regressor metrics (MSE, RMSE, R²)
Classification model for process-variation-aware device identification
Faster alternative to TCAD simulation for device characterization
Foundation for interdisciplinary semiconductor design-ML collaboration

metrics.accuracy_metrics: MSE, RMSE, R² (specific values not provided)
